chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih who said:

I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that my paternal aunt is with me and she is my colleague, and the heat is intense upon her when she wears Ihraam. So, what is your view for me if I were to shade upon myself and upon her? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Shade upon her alone'.

key_terms.أَحْرَمَتْ: She entered the state of Ihraam (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.أُظَلِّلَ: To shade/cover with a shadow or cloth
key_terms.زَمِيلَتِي: My colleague/companion (one who travels with me)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shading a woman in Ihraam during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of shading during Ihraam by distinguishing between the general allowance for men and the specific ruling for women. While a man may shade himself, the Imam instructs that the female relative be shaded separately, reflecting scholarly discussions on whether the prohibition of shading applies equally to men and women or if there are distinctions in how the heat's intensity affects their respective states of ritual purity and modesty.
